title: Opacity-modified text tokens fail AA on income, calendar and settings
description: text-rizq-ink-soft/60 cannot reach 4.5:1 on any light surface: /ar/income shows 21 failing nodes, all of them the delivery date and status caption on every gig card. /ar/calendar has 5 (a /50 overflow count and three filter chips), /ar/settings 1 (حذف الحساب). Same class as RZQ-0002, which was filed for /ar/dashboard alone because that is the only route the sweep ran axe against. The design system already has --content-faint for exactly this, darkened to clear AA; the opacity modifier bypasses it.

/ar/income: 21 color-contrast nodes, e.g.

note: --warn darkened #94671f -> #805614 (4.24:1 -> 5.49:1 on --raised, 4.73:1 on --bg) and the three /40 caption texts moved to the --content-faint token that already exists for muted copy. /ar/dashboard reports 0 color-contrast nodes under axe wcag2aa. The same class on other routes is filed as RZQ-0013.

One shared fmtMoney keeps halalas when the amount has them and stays whole when it does not; AnimatedNumber pins the digit count to its target so a count-up does not tick in halalas. Verified on the 9,938.21 invoice: header strip, artifact, list card and og description all read ٩٬٩٣٨٫٢١, and dashboard/income whole figures are unchanged.

One fmtRate owns the rule; the invoice builders VAT line reads (١٥%) matching the toggle above it, and the fee-rate line beside it. The blind spot the finding named is closed by a static guard (src/lib/format/rate.test.ts) that reads the source instead of driving the app — it found 9 more raw percentages the sweep could never reach, all fixed. No Latin percentage remains on any Arabic route swept.

The four controls that failed the WCAG 2.5.8 AA minimum (24x24) are fixed: insights collapse 107x20 -> 107x24, refresh 48x16 -> 56x24, both vote buttons 20x20 -> 24x24, locale toggle 94x16 -> 94x24. The rest of the 21 are 32-40px shell controls that PASS AA and miss only the AAA 44px target; taking the whole header and sidebar to 44px changes the shell layout, which is a design-system call for the founder, not a fix to apply unasked.

Captions moved off the opacity idiom onto --content-muted/--content-faint, --over darkened #be4326 -> #a5391f (3.89:1 -> 4.88:1 on its own soft fill), and the calendar day-number ternary fixed — it applied the muted colour when isToday was true as well, so todays date read 1.25:1 on its own green pill. axe wcag2aa now reports 0 color-contrast nodes on income, calendar, settings, dashboard, invoices, clients, projects and proposals.

title: /ar/income fails AA contrast on mobile only — month label and the log-income chip
description: At 390x844 axe reports two serious color-contrast nodes that are clean at 1280x900, which is why the desktop verification that closed RZQ-0013 missed them and why the sweep kept re-filing them under RZQ-0002 (a reference whose title names /ar/dashboard). (a) the month label uses text-rizq-ink-soft/60 on --raised = 3.19:1 — the same opacity idiom RZQ-0013 replaced elsewhere. (b) the log-income chip is text --acc over bg-rizq-green/8, and 8% green is translucent, so its effective background is whatever surface sits behind it: --raised on desktop (passes) and --bg on mobile (4.43:1, fails). The chip pattern is the more important half — its contrast changes with layout, so it can pass review and fail in production.

REOPENED. Recurred on cycle 3 row 45 against the PRODUCTION build, nowhere near a server fault — so the needs-repro reasoning (that it was the dev server dying) is falsified. My hand-reproduction showed the quota refusal working (gigs 20->20, dialog visible); that was evidence the path CAN work, not that it always does. Intermittent: 2 occurrences in ~200 dev rows, 1 in ~145 production rows. Symptom stands as filed — an income save left no gig row and no dialog, so the freelancer got neither saved work nor an explanation.

Cause found by targeted repro (2 silent failures in 30 submits): the server-action POST to /ar/income/new is aborted mid-flight — net::ERR_ABORTED alongside 17 aborted RSC prefetches, saturating the HTTP/1.1 connection pool — and GigForm awaited createGig/updateGig with no try/catch, so the rejection left isPending cleared, error null, and the freelancer staring at a filled form. Both branches now catch and show a message that deliberately does NOT say try again, because an aborted response may still have reached the server and a blind retry on the money path logs income twice. Verified in a browser by aborting the POST deliberately (message shown, no row), plus the quota refusal still explaining itself and a real save still succeeding 19->20.

title: A server action that throws leaves 47 forms silent
description: RZQ-0015 was one instance of a pattern. 55 components call a server action inside startTransition and only 8 have any try/catch, so whenever the request is aborted or the action throws, the promise rejects, isPending clears and nothing is shown — the user cannot tell whether their work was saved. Measured at roughly 7% of submits under load on /ar/income/new, caused by RSC prefetches saturating the connection pool. GigForm is fixed; ClientForm, InvoiceForm, ItemForm, FeeForm, the auth forms and the rest are not. The lasting fix is one wrapper every form calls rather than 47 copies of the same try/catch, and it should say what GigForm now says: the save is unconfirmed, check before retrying.
evidence: measured 2 silent failures in 30 submits on /ar/income/new
requestfailed: /ar/income/new net::ERR_ABORTED with 17 concurrent ?_rsc= prefetch aborts

note: Shared wrapper lib/actions/attempt.ts + Common.saveUnconfirmed, applied to the forms that write money and client data: ClientForm, InvoiceForm, ItemForm, FeeForm (GigForm was done under RZQ-0015). Guarded components went 8 -> 12 of 55. Verified in a browser by aborting the action POST: /ar/clients/new now shows the message instead of throwing the page to the error boundary, /ar/catalog shows it instead of nothing (abort and empty items table both confirmed), and a normal client save still navigates 8 -> 9 to /ar/clients/{id}. One correction to the original filing: not every form went silent — ClientForm escalated to the global error boundary and lost the typed input, which is a different symptom of the same unhandled rejection.

title: The remaining 43 forms still have no guard on a failed action
description: RZQ-0023 put a shared wrapper (lib/actions/attempt) behind the money and client-data forms, taking guarded components from 8 to 12 of 55. The rest still let a rejected action unwind the transition: 10 onboarding steps, 9 auth forms, 7 project components, 5 proposal components, 3 settings, and one each in upgrade, tool, methodology, landing, invoices, income, documents, clients and admin. Consequence varies by form — some show nothing, some lose the page to the error boundary — but none tell the user whether the write landed. Onboarding and auth matter most of what is left: a signup or an onboarding step that silently fails strands someone before they ever reach the product. The wrapper exists; this is applying it, plus one message per namespace or a shared Common string.
